mechanism_claims.claim_text: DLP-PH has source-supported membrane-interaction/permeabilization evidence, including E. coli membrane docking context and cytoplasmic material release assays; the final interpretation remains cautious because the paper itself discusses possible non-lytic contributions at MIC for E. coli and C. albicans.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Docking is computational and leakage is not sufficient alone for all organisms; do not overclaim a single pore-formation mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: DLP-PH has anti-biofilm activity measurements, but the paper reports weaker activity against established sessile biofilms than against planktonic cells and frames P. aeruginosa initial-attachment inhibition as a possible non-lethal attachment effect.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Anti-biofilm measurements support functional activity and a cautious hypothesis, not definitive biofilm eradication mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: DLP-PH shows anti-proliferative activity against H-157 and PC-3 with lower toxicity toward HMEC-1; the paper proposes membrane-charge related selectivity as a hypothesis rather than a proven cancer-cell molecular target.
